usability-ux-universal-design.why: the change extends this skill's plain-language rule from UI copy to an agent's own reports: measure the reading grade before sending, and keep the evidence words when simplifying.
usability-ux-universal-design.what: added scripts/readability.mjs (Flesch-Kincaid, prose only, --max-grade gate), a Step 4 bullet, a mechanical-gate note, two evidence-ledger rows, a done-checklist line, and a 'Reports to people' section in content-and-plain-language.md.
quotes: Words are UI, and people skim rather than read

skeptical-audit.why: the change adds the evidence-words rule (keep counts/totals, chosen vs random, the evidence state; never reframe a fixed set as tries/odds/rate) to this skill's evidence discipline.
skeptical-audit.what: added section 8 to the evidence contract, the EVIDENCE-WORDS claim-lint rule (numeric framing + same-line co-occurrence, affirmative-random only), and a meta-check note in SKILL.md.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

verifiable-quality-gates.why: both new checks (readability.mjs and the EVIDENCE-WORDS claim-lint rule) must provably detect what they claim, so each ships a committed test that fails if the check is no-opped.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added discriminating tests: readability flags an over-grade draft and fails closed on a missing/bad target; the EVIDENCE-WORDS rule flags the chosen-set-as-tries/odds/rate slip and passes the no-FP cases the review found.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the two issue behaviors (report meets the grade; simplifying keeps the evidence words) are enumerated as operator scenarios, stored in the datastore, logged, and run on the executable harness.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added two @audience:operator scenarios to features/evidence/claims-match-evidence.feature with step defs that drive the real scripts; regenerated bdd-index.json/INDEX.md; appended the coverage log.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the behavior-change coupling requires tests at the lowest level that can catch the bug, so both scripts get unit tests over fixtures, not only the end-to-end scenarios.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/readability.test.mjs and extended test/claim-lint.test.mjs with the rule's bad/good/no-FP unit cases, at the script level.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

architectural-decision-records.why: the decision of where each rule lives (reading grade in usability-ux, evidence words in skeptical-audit) and why a readability script is justified is recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: added docs/adr/0094-reading-grade-and-evidence-words.md (context, considered options, decision, consequences with honest limits) and a CHANGELOG entry.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

pattern-selector.why: the design choice was made on purpose: a single dependency-free CLI script and a rule added to the existing linter, with no new abstraction (factory/manager/interface) for a single use.
pattern-selector.what: chose no new pattern: readability.mjs is a plain script, and the evidence-words rule extends claim-lint rather than introducing a parallel checker, matching the surrounding code.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review ran on the diff before this receipt; it raised three violations and two minor items, all fixed, and the review is recorded in the arch-review log.
judge-arch.what: dispatched the four-questions review to a general-purpose subagent in fresh context; fixed the cry-wolf FPs, the --max-grade fail-open, the dead random branch, and the overstated wording.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: offline evidence-discipline and readability tooling over repo-local trusted text; no untrusted input, auth, session, secret, network, or deserialization surface.

arch-encode.why: the audit behaviors are encoded as a claim-lint rule and the evidence contract, following the established skill pattern, not as a new arch-gate config rule.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, storage, retention, migration, or backup is touched.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no running system, service boundary, data model, or scaling surface; two small CLI reference scripts and docs.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature flag, or rollback of a running system.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, SLO, alert, or golden signal.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no rendered UI or .tsx/.jsx/.html/.css surface; the reading-grade concern is content-level and handled by usability-ux.
